Status.note: The EIA-860M table for September 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/electricity/data/eia860m/xls/september_generator2026.xlsx) lists Jack Watson, plant 2049, generator 4 as operating. The unit now burns natural gas.

Conversion/replacement?.note: An Associated Press article carried by Mississippi Public Broadcasting in 2015 (https://www.mpbonline.org/blogs/news/mississippi-powers-conversion-of-plant-nearly-complete/) says Mississippi Power would convert Plant Watson units 4 and 5 from coal to natural gas, with the work finished by April 16, 2015.

Start year.note: The same 2015 article says the conversion to natural gas should be complete by April 16, 2015. So the start year of the gas unit is 2015. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 gives 1968 for unit 4 and 1973 for unit 5. Those are the years the original coal units began operating, so GEM's 2015 for the converted gas unit is right. A saved copy of the Transmission Hub article of February 27, 2015, which is already a source in GEM, says the same: Plant Watson would burn natural gas only by April 16, 2015. The live address now opens the TD World home page, so the saved copy is cited.

Planned retire.note: Southern Company's annual report for 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/92122/000009212226000006/so-20251231.htm) says Mississippi Power's 2024 resource plan schedules Plant Watson Unit 4, 268 MW, to retire by the end of 2028. The same report says Mississippi Power told the state regulator in January 2025 that it may extend the retirement dates of some steam units beyond 2028 to serve new large loads. The date may therefore move.

units.notes: Unit 4 is operating on natural gas. Southern Company's 2025 annual report shows a planned retirement by the end of 2028, which may be extended. Latitude.note: The air permit at https://opcgis.deq.state.ms.us/ensearchonline/get_doc.aspx?dt=finalp&id=1583174 gives the plant address as 10406 Lorraine Road, Gulfport, Mississippi 39503. The Census geocoder puts that address at 30.44115, -89.03097, about half a kilometer from GEM's point. A satellite picture of GEM's point at 30.43923, -89.02611 (imagery date unknown) shows the plant itself, with the boiler house, stacks, switchyard and cooling canal under the crosshair.
